answer: Quadratic cost scaling at the opal: each additional identity a farm registers multiplies required stake by n², so n identities demand n² locked capital. The summit of viable farming caps near ten identities, where marginal revenue flattens against the quadratic curve. A thread of linked wallets is detectable because honest stake grows linearly while sybil stake grows quadratically. Break-even: an attacker with capital C can sustain only sqrt(C) identities before returns go negative, so scaling past that point costs more than any Byzantine gain.
